findings.title: Mercy as continuing provision and care
findings.claim: Across the declared surah context, the mercy named in 1:3 is joined to progressive nurture, practical help, repair, guardianship, and bestowed well-being, so compassion becomes an ongoing care relation rather than an isolated feeling.
findings.mechanism: The focus pair carries beneficent mercy; Rabb's nurture, the request for assistance, the care-and-preservation image, the provision-and-repair image, and the favor image provide separate contextual carriers that turn tenderness into sustained maintenance of a dependent toward good condition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive mercy as something that acts through feeding, helping, guarding, repairing, and stabilizing a dependent, not only as an inward quality.
findings.containment: The ordinary meaning of the two divine mercy names remains intact. This is a whole-surah contextual care relation, and it does not assert that every available branch of any cited root is active.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel supports explicitly name the focus and contextual carriers and their care-process connection; the synthesis is bounded to the declared pericope.
